# oncebitten

oncebitten turns repeated agent mistakes into rules that git enforces. A rule is a directory. `oncebitten check` runs the active rules against changed files and reports findings.

## Commands

- `oncebitten check [--base <rev>]`: run each `active` block rule against changes since `<rev>` (default `HEAD`). Changes are the tracked diff plus untracked files. Exit 0 clean, 1 a rule fired, 2 a rule could not run or rules did not load (2 wins over 1). Findings print to stdout as `<id>: <path>[:<line>]: <message>`. Could-not-run reasons print to stderr as `<id>: could not run: <reason>`.
- `oncebitten replay --stale` replays every active or proposed project rule whose proof is missing or stale (exit 0 all proven, 1 any rejected, 2 any could not run). `oncebitten replay <rule-id> [--checker <path>] [--gateway <endpoint>] [--local]`: replay an ast-grep or diff rule (fires on `fixtures/bad.*`, clean on `fixtures/fixed.*` and `corpus/`) in an OpenShell sandbox; a steer rule replays with the in-process matcher and its proof names `"backend": "matcher"`. A proven verdict writes `proof.json` into the rule directory; commit it. Exit 0 proven, 1 rejected, 2 could not run. `--local` runs without a sandbox and writes no proof.
- `oncebitten gate pr --base <target>` (CI) and `oncebitten gate pre-push [--base <ref>]` (pre-push hook): run `active` `block` rules on the paths changed since the merge-base (pre-push: `PRE_COMMIT_FROM_REF`..`PRE_COMMIT_TO_REF`). `pr` needs `rules.lock` and a valid `proof.json` for each gated ast-grep or diff rule and each active steer rule; `pre-push` only warns about proofs. Findings listed in `.oncebitten/baseline.json` pass. Exit 0 clean, 1 a new violation, 2 could not run. `gate pr` also accepts an attachment link in the PR description or comments as evidence for a diff rule. Details: docs/gate.md. The pre-push hook needs the pre-commit framework: hook id `oncebitten-gate` from this repo, `pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push`. CI templates: templates/.
- `oncebitten baseline update`: replace `.oncebitten/baseline.json` with the current violations of active block rules in every tracked file (sorted JSON). Diff rules are not baselined; a native rule is baselined by id alone. Exit 0 written, 2 a rule could not run.
- `oncebitten steer --host <claude|codex|cursor|copilot|opencode|pi>`: agent hook. Reads the host payload on stdin, matches active steer rules and prints the host's inform or deny output; prints nothing when none match. Always exits 0; honours `ONCEBITTEN_TRIAGE=1`. `oncebitten hooks install|uninstall --host <h> --scope <user|project>` writes or removes it beside the capture hook. Cursor and copilot can only deny tool calls; pi informs on a tool call only after the turn. Details: docs/steer.md.
- `oncebitten rules sync [--frozen]`: clone each source to the data directory and write `.oncebitten/rules.lock`. `--frozen` checks out the locked commits, fetching only a commit the clone lacks, and never writes the lock; exit 2 when it cannot. CI runs `--frozen` before `gate pr`.
- `oncebitten rules list [--ci]`: print `id  mode  status  origin` per rule.
- `oncebitten rules retire <id> --reason <text>`: set `status = "retired"` and `retired_reason` on a project rule. A retired rule never runs and needs no proof; `baseline update` drops its entries. A source rule exits 2: retire it in its rules repo or override it. Details: docs/lifecycle.md.
- `oncebitten rules rollback <id>`: return an active project rule to `proposed`, keeping its files and proof; prints `git log` and `git restore --source <commit>` commands for the rule directory. Exit 2 when the rule is not an active project rule.
- `oncebitten exception add <rule> --paths <glob>... --reason <text> --expires <YYYY-MM-DD>` and `oncebitten exception list`: manage `.oncebitten/exceptions.toml`. `check` and `gate` drop findings a live exception covers and print the count; an exception expires the day after `expires`, and `gate` warns about each expired one. All four keys are required; `paths = ["**"]` covers every path. An invalid file exits 2.
- `oncebitten doctor [--gateway <endpoint>]`: read-only checks (config, pre-commit >= 3.2.0 and the gate hook, rules.lock, rules and proofs, exceptions, capture hooks per installed host, evidence store, OpenShell), one `ok|warn|fail  <check>: <message> (fix: ...)` line each. Exit 0 no fail, 1 any fail. Details: docs/doctor.md.
- `oncebitten rules validate [--ci]`: load and resolve every rule.
- `oncebitten triage <cluster-id> [--host <host>]`: ask the configured host (claude, codex or opencode; pi is unsupported) for a one-shot JSON verdict on an evidence cluster. Prints `{repeatable, user_correction, root_cause, proposed_fix_kind, generality}` to stdout. A rule-shaped verdict also drafts a rule, written to `.oncebitten/rules/<id>/` with `status = "proposed"` and replayed. Runs in an empty temp dir with `ONCEBITTEN_TRIAGE=1`. Sends the session's changed code hunks to the triage host unless `triage.send_code = false`; an ast-grep or native draft's `bad` fixture must quote a consecutive post-image run of one hunk that includes a substantive (not blank, not lone-brace) added line, else exit 2; diff drafts are exempt. Claude and codex must pass a hooks-off proof; opencode does not. Over the daily budget it still runs and warns on stderr. Exit 0 verdict, 2 could not run. Details: docs/triage.md.
- `oncebitten proposals list|show <id>|accept <id>|reject <id> --reason <text>|deliver <id> [--to pr|rules-repo] [--push]`: review drafted rules, keyed by evidence cluster id; `list` and `show` print the existing hits of an ast-grep rule at HEAD (count, samples; informational, never blocks). `accept` activates a proposal only with a valid `proof.json`, else exit 2, and baselines the rule's existing hits in `.oncebitten/baseline.json`. `accept <id> --deny` sets a steer proposal's action to deny and re-proves it; exit 2 for non-steer proposals. `reject` also rejects the cluster; `reject <id> --duplicate-of <other>` records a confirmed duplicate instead of `--reason`. Recorded proposals flag `possible duplicate of <id> (<reason>)` on equal `mistake_class` or token Jaccard >= 0.5, in `list`, `show` and the PR body. `capture` starts triage in the background when a cluster reaches its threshold (`triage.background = false` turns it off; `triage.max_per_day`, default 10, caps background runs per local day and records `skipped: budget` rows in `triage_runs`; a later capture in the same repo starts those clusters once under the cap; `triggers.session` lists the session signals that may start a background run). A background run that fails stores its error, and `proposals list` prints `triage failed for <id> (<host>): <error>` to stderr until a later run or a proposal replaces it. The gate prints a non-blocking notice when proposals wait. `deliver` commits the rule to the current branch (`pr`) or to a branch of the `writable = true` rules source (`rules-repo`), with `--push` pushing and opening a PR through `gh`, `glab` or `az`; it never activates. Details: docs/proposals.md.
- `oncebitten stats [--since <days>] [--json]`: read-only funnel per mistake class: signals captured, clusters at threshold, rule-shaped drafts, proven, accepted, rejected, waiting. `triage runs` is n/a (not recorded). Missing store prints `no data` and exits 0; never creates it. Details: docs/stats.md.
- `oncebitten config show|path`: show merged configuration.

## Rule layers

Precedence, highest first: project `.oncebitten/rules/<id>/`, then sources in config order, then shipped examples (only those listed in `rules.use_examples`). A project rule with the id of a source rule needs `overrides = "<source>/<id>"` and a `reason`.

## Rule directory

```
<rule-id>/
  rule.toml
  check.yml          # ast-grep only
  fixtures/
    bad.<ext>        # exactly one
    fixed.<ext>      # exactly one; diff rules use bad.diff and fixed.diff, steer rules bad.json and fixed.json
  corpus/            # replay only: files that must stay clean
  proof.json         # written by a proven OpenShell replay; not part of the hash
```

`rule.toml` fields: `id` (equal to the directory name), `description`, `mode` (`block` or `steer`), `status` (`proposed`, `active`, `retired`; only `active` runs in `check` and `gate`), `retired_reason` (optional, non-empty), `engine` (`ast-grep`, `native`, `diff`, `steer`), `language` (optional), `overrides` and `reason`, `command` (native), `fired_exit_codes` (native, non-zero integers), `fired_output_contains` (native, with `fired_exit_codes`; fires only when stdout or stderr contains this text), `when_changed` and `require_changed` (diff, non-empty glob arrays), `[steer]` (steer: `action` `inform` or `deny`, `message`, `[steer.trigger]` with one of `tool` plus optional `command` regex, `paths` globs, `prompt` regex; `deny` needs `tool`). Unknown keys fail the load.

## Engines

- `ast-grep`: `check.yml` is an ast-grep rule. Runs on changed files whose language ast-grep recognises. Matches syntax only: no types, and macro arguments are not visible.
- `native`: runs `command` in the repository root. Exit 0 is clean. An exit code in `fired_exit_codes` is fired, and its output is the message. Any other exit code, a missing binary or a signal is could-not-run. With `fired_output_contains`, a listed exit code is fired only when the output contains that text; otherwise could-not-run.
- `steer`: needs `mode = "steer"`. Not run by `check` or `gate`; the `oncebitten steer` hook matches it against agent tool calls and prompts. Fixtures are normalized events, e.g. `{"event": "tool", "tool": "Bash", "command": "sudo ls"}`, `{"event": "tool", "tool": "Write", "paths": ["src/gen/a.rs"]}`, `{"event": "prompt", "prompt": "..."}`.
- `diff`: fires when a `when_changed` glob matches a changed path and no `require_changed` glob matches any changed path. Globs use `*` within one directory and `**` across directories.

## Shipped examples (opt-in: list ids in `rules.use_examples`; a listed example is active)

`py-utcnow`, `py-no-print`, `js-moment`, `ts-no-as-any` (ast-grep); `rust-no-unwrap` (native: `cargo clippy --message-format=json -- -D clippy::unwrap_used`, fired on exit 101 with `"code":"clippy::unwrap_used"` in the output); `arch-diagram`, `ui-screenshot` (diff); `no-sudo` (steer: denies shell commands matching `^\s*sudo\b`).

## Example rule

```toml
id = "ui-screenshot"
description = "UI changes need a screenshot."
mode = "block"
status = "active"
engine = "diff"
when_changed = ["src/ui/**"]
require_changed = ["docs/screenshots/*.png"]
```
